name: Gwŷr y Gogledd
text: Gwŷr y Gogledd is the Welsh name for the men of the north. The term marks the P-Celtic Britons who lived in the north of Britain. These peoples were the forebears of the Welsh in speech and custom. Yet their lands ceased to be part of Wales. Many of them dwelt in kingdoms that no longer stand, such as Gododdin, Rheged, and Strathclyde. Those territories now lie within the Lowlands of Scotland. The Welsh phrase can also mean the men of the left. The peoples of Gwŷr y Gogledd therefore join the early Welsh to the wider British past.
